record.title: Control override and ordered patch semantics
record.selected_analysis: Set computes value*scale+offset; mul/add acts on all animation numeric values as described. Controls override bound values; patching a bound field moves controlling slider. Plain-number subfield binding guidance and mul animation option differ. Ordered patch prose names twelve operations; conditional invalid-path, conflict and transaction behavior is not a formal schema. Controls: {"id", "label", "type": "slider"|"toggle"|"select"|"ramp", "value", "binds": [path | {"path", "scale", "offset", "mode": "set"|"mul"|"add"}], "min", "max", "step" (slider), "options" (select: [{"label","value"}]; ramp: preset names or colour lists)}.
  A slider writes value*scale+offset into every bound path (mode set, the default). Paths: layers.<id>.<field>, into animated values (layers.ring.radius.to, layers.fx.intensity.keys.2.1, layers.aura.radius.wave.mid), subject.<field>, ramps.<name> (ramp control, value = a preset name or colour list), camera.tilt, outline.mode, dither, tones, detail, seed. mode mul multiplies the WHOLE bound value (a number or every number of an animation: from/to, every key, a wave's mid and amp) by value*scale+offset, so an animated field keeps its animation and gets a size slider (a 0.5..1.5 slider = half to one and a half); mode add adds it instead. Toggles bind layers.<id>.enabled. Controls override the values they bind. The user drags them anywhere, so every position must stay valid (both slider ends inside the bound field's range), and one control sets each value. Any layer may carry a "group" name (layers that belong together; remove_group removes them). A layer may name a preset ramp it did not declare ("ramp": "frost").

- A slider binds plain numbers: inside an animated value bind .to / .from / .keys.<i>.1 / .wave.mid.
- If the effect is cut off at the edges or floats in a lot of empty space, render(fit_canvas=true) resizes the canvas around it (everything moves; the reply tells you by how much).
- When an error says "did you mean", use that name.
- Sliders win: a value a control writes always renders as the control says. Patching such a value moves that control (the reply tells you); to animate a slider-driven value, bind it with "mode": "mul" so the slider scales the whole animation.

patch = list of ops applied in order to your working recipe ([] renders it as is): {"op": "set", "path": "layers.circle.radius", "value": 40} (any path: layers.<id>.<field>[.from|.keys.1.1], controls.<id>.value, camera.tilt, ramps.main, frames ...); {"op": "remove", "path": "layers.sparks.wobble"}; {"op": "add_layer", "layer": {...}, "after": "<id>"} (or "before"; default: on top); {"op": "replace_layer", "layer": {...}}; {"op": "remove_layer", "id": "<id>"}; {"op": "add_control", "control": {...}}; {"op": "replace_control", "control": {...}}; {"op": "remove_control", "id": "<id>"}; {"op": "remove_group", "group": "<name>"} (every layer with that group, and their sliders); {"op": "retime", "frames": N, "keep": "duration"|"speed"} (duration: fps follows; life windows land on frames) or {"op": "retime", "lead_in": k} (k frames before everything, one-shots); {"op": "scale", "factor": 0.5, "about": [x, y]} (positions, radii, widths, speeds and their sliders; about defaults to the origin; the sprite keeps its size); {"op": "move", "group": "<name>", "by": [dx, dy]} (a group's positions and the sliders that write them). record.title: Projection/subject effects restrict pixel-preservation claims
record.selected_analysis: Quarter-turn/mirror source transform claims are local, not whole-effect RGBA preservation. Light recolors subject, ignores z/plane; subject tint/wave/shore/echo explicitly alter appearance or placement. Camera prescriptions are documented geometry, without full raster rounding/projection code.

record.title: Export saves state and rerenders pieces
record.selected_analysis: Export saves My effects, can replace saved effect and supplies interoperable image ID plus GIF/sheetJSON. Game pack adds clips and manifest and rerenders pieces; part selects one piece. The docs do not define pivots, clocks, subject inclusion, URLs or replace atomicity. No export invoked and no billing verified; no-generation/no-charge prose is not attested implementation.

sources.verbatim_selected_text: vfx_workbench: you are the effects artist; our renderer draws crisp pixel-art VFX from what you build (tuned parts with sliders, and your own layers in a JSON recipe). Nothing is generated on our side and nothing is charged: you design, it renders, you LOOK at every reply's frames and correct.

- <step id> export [--name <name>] [--replace <My effects id>] [--game-pack | --part <part id>] -> saves it to the user's My effects (they open it on pixellab.ai, move its sliders, ask the website's artist for changes) and returns a GIF and a spritesheet PNG + JSON, plus an image id the pixelart_workbench and save_to_asset take. --game-pack adds a ZIP for a game engine: every piece as its own clip (the whole effect, behind and in front of the sprite, each part) + manifest.json saying where each plays; --part <id> just one piece (a projectile, an impact). Ask for them only when the user wants pieces: they render every part again. Export again with --replace to update it.

5. Beats: in an effect with several beats (a cast, a projectile, its impact, what lingers), give each part its role (add_part / set_part role=...). The user exports the effect for their game in pieces, one clip per part, and the roles say which clip plays where (the projectile's clip comes out in place, for the game to move).
5b. Core: mark what makes the effect what the user asked for (the fire of a fireball, the bolt of a lightning strike, the ring of a magic circle) with add_part core=true, or list layer ids / part ids in the recipe's "core". The page's Reroll varies everything and may turn any other piece off; the core always stays.
6. Sliders: parts bring theirs (labelled with the part's name). Add your own only for something the user will want that they don't cover; check with render(check_controls=true).
7. export saves the effect to the user's My effects and hands over its files: ['<step id>', 'export', '--name', '<name>']. Tell the user in plain words what you made, which sliders to try, and that they can open it on pixellab.ai (the reply's link).
Changes later: continue from the last step id (an earlier one is a way back), or `start --effect <My effects id>` for a saved effect (it carries the slider values the user set on the website). Change what they asked for, keep the rest, then export with --replace <that id> to update it in place.

func generate() -> void :
	var required_size = _get_canvas_size_for_tool()
	var tile_w: int = required_size.x
	var tile_h: int = required_size.y
	var canvas = ExtensionsApi.project.current_project.size
	if canvas.x != tile_w or canvas.y != tile_h:
		var dialog = AcceptDialog.new()
		dialog.title = "Canvas size mismatch"
		dialog.dialog_text = "Canvas size (%dx%d) does not match selected tile size (%dx%d). Generate anyway?" % [canvas.x, canvas.y, tile_w, tile_h]
		dialog.get_ok_button().hide()
		dialog.add_theme_constant_override("buttons_separation", 12)
		dialog.add_theme_constant_override("buttons_min_width", 140)
		dialog.add_button("Cancel", false, "cancel")
		dialog.add_button("Generate anyway", true, "generate")
		dialog.connect("custom_action", func(action: String):
			dialog.queue_free()
			if action == "generate":
				super.generate()
		)
		dialog.connect("close_requested", dialog.queue_free)
		ExtensionsApi.dialog.get_dialogs_parent_node().add_child(dialog)
		dialog.popup_centered()
		return
	super.generate()

local function get_number_of_frames(target_size)
  if target_size <= 64 then
    return 16 -- 32x32 or 64x64 -> 16 frames
  else
    return 4  -- 128x128 or 256x256 -> 4 frames
  end
end

-- Helper function to determine target dimensions (preserves aspect ratio)
local function calculate_target_dimensions(width, height)
  local max_dim = math.max(width, height)
  local target_max

  if max_dim <= 32 then
    target_max = 32
  elseif max_dim <= 64 then
    target_max = 64
  elseif max_dim <= 128 then
    target_max = 128
  elseif max_dim <= 256 and _tier >= 2 then
    target_max = 256
  else
    -- Default to max allowed size
    if _tier >= 2 then
      target_max = 256
    else
      target_max = 128
    end
  end

  -- If both dimensions fit within target_max, use original dimensions
  if width <= target_max and height <= target_max then
    return width, height
  end

  -- Scale down to fit within target_max
  local scale = target_max / max_dim
  return math.floor(width * scale), math.floor(height * scale)
end

-- Helper function to determine target size based on max dimension
local function calculate_target_size(width, height)
    local max_dim = math.max(width, height)
    local target_size

    if max_dim <= 32 then
        target_size = 32
    elseif max_dim <= 64 then
        target_size = 64
    elseif max_dim <= 128 then
        target_size = 128
    elseif max_dim <= 256 and _tier >= 2 then
        target_size = 256
    else
        if _tier >= 2 then
            target_size = 256
        else
            target_size = 128
        end
    end

    return target_size
end

-- Helper function to pad an image to target size
local function pad_image(image, target_size)
    local width = image.width
    local height = image.height

    if width == target_size and height == target_size then
        return image:clone()
    end

    local pad_x = math.floor((target_size - width) / 2)
    local pad_y = math.floor((target_size - height) / 2)

    -- Create new image with target size (RGB mode)
    local padded_image = Image(target_size, target_size, ColorMode.RGB)

    -- Draw original image in the center
    padded_image:drawImage(image, Point(pad_x, pad_y))

    return padded_image
end

local function convert_points_to_api_format(points, width, height, direction)
  local api_points = {}
  local processed_labels = {}

  for _, point in ipairs(points) do
    if not processed_labels[point.label] then
      processed_labels[point.label] = true
      table.insert(api_points, {
        x = point.x / width,
        y = point.y / height,
        label = point.label,
        z_index = point.z_index or 0,
        depth = get_depth_for_label(point.label, direction)
      })
    end
  end

  return api_points
end

-- Helper: Create frozen mask (black = don't regenerate, use as reference)
-- Raw RGBA bytes, all black pixels
local function create_frozen_mask(width, height)
  local size = width * height * 4 -- RGBA = 4 bytes per pixel
  local bytes = {}
  for i = 1, size, 4 do
    bytes[i] = 0       -- R = 0 (black)
    bytes[i + 1] = 0   -- G = 0
    bytes[i + 2] = 0   -- B = 0
    bytes[i + 3] = 255 -- A = 255 (opaque)
  end
  return base64.encode(string.char(table.unpack(bytes)))
end

-- Helper: Create inpainted mask (white = regenerate this area)
-- Raw RGBA bytes, all white pixels
local function create_inpainted_mask(width, height)
  local size = width * height * 4
  local bytes = {}
  for i = 1, size, 4 do
    bytes[i] = 255     -- R = 255 (white)
    bytes[i + 1] = 255 -- G = 255
    bytes[i + 2] = 255 -- B = 255
    bytes[i + 3] = 255 -- A = 255 (opaque)
  end
  return base64.encode(string.char(table.unpack(bytes)))
end

    bytes[i + 2] = 0   -- B = 0

local function export_pose(frame_number, width, height)
  -- A partially erased pose may fall back to saved cel properties. Treat
  -- malformed properties as an invalid pose, including in the preview.
  local ok, points = pcall(get_pose_from_frame_number, frame_number, false)
  if not ok or type(points) ~= "table" then return nil end

  local keypoints, valid_points = {}, {}
  -- The pose reader can recover partial poses from cel properties. Require each
  -- distinct API label, not just a count of pixels in the skeleton layer.
  for _, info in pairs(handle_pose.points_information) do
    local point = points[info.label]
    if type(point) ~= "table" or type(point.x) ~= "number" or type(point.y) ~= "number"
        or not (point.x >= 0 and point.x <= width and point.y >= 0 and point.y <= height) then
      return nil
    end
    local z_index = point.z_index
    if z_index == nil then z_index = 0 end
    if type(z_index) ~= "number" or z_index % 1 ~= 0 then return nil end
    valid_points[info.label] = point
    keypoints[#keypoints + 1] = {
      label = info.label,
      x = point.x / width,
      y = point.y / height,
      z_index = z_index
      -- Omit depth: the API derives it from the body's standing template.
    }
  end
  if #keypoints ~= 18 then return nil end
  table.sort(keypoints, function(a, b) return a.label < b.label end)
  return keypoints, valid_points

function generate_movement.generate(model, dlg_type)
  local request_history_data = createJson.deepcopy(model.current_json)
  if generatingImage then
    return app.alert("Already generating")
  end
  if app.activeSprite == nil then
    return app.alert("Must have an active canvas")
  end
  if model.current_json["use_selection"] then
    model.current_json["selection_origin"][1] = app.activeSprite.selection.origin.x
    model.current_json["selection_origin"][2] = app.activeSprite.selection.origin.y
  end

  if model.current_json["use_selection"] and (app.activeSprite.selection.bounds.width ~= 64 or app.activeSprite.selection.bounds.height ~= 64) then
    return app.alert("Selection width and height must be equal to 64")
  elseif model.current_json["use_selection"] == false and (app.activeSprite.width ~= 64 or app.activeSprite.height ~= 64) then
    -- Check if canvas can be padded to 64x64 (only if smaller than 64x64)
    if app.activeSprite.width <= 64 and app.activeSprite.height <= 64 then
      if ask_auto_pad_to_64_dialog(app.activeSprite.width, app.activeSprite.height) then
        -- User agreed to pad - expand canvas to 64x64 and center content
        local current_width = app.activeSprite.width
        local current_height = app.activeSprite.height
        local x_offset = math.floor((64 - current_width) / 2)
        local y_offset = math.floor((64 - current_height) / 2)

        app.activeSprite:crop(-x_offset, -y_offset, 64, 64)
        app.refresh()

        -- After padding, cancel generation so user can update their reference image if needed
        return app.alert("Canvas has been padded to 64x64. Please set your reference image again and retry generation.")
      else
        return -- User cancelled
      end
    else
      return app.alert("Canvas width and height must be equal to 64")
    end
  elseif model.current_json["selected_reference_image"] ~= nil and model.current_json["selected_reference_image"] ~= "" and (model.current_json["selected_reference_image"].width ~= 64 or model.current_json["selected_reference_image"].height ~= 64) then
    return app.alert("Reference width and height must be equal to 64")
  end
  local data_images = getImage.get_images_from_model_from_json(model.current_json)
  local no_inpaint = 0
  for index = 1, 4 do
    if data_images["inpainting_images"][index] ~= nil and data_images["inpainting_images"][index] ~= "" and data_images["inpainting_images"][index]:isPlain(Color { r = 0, g = 0, b = 0, a = 255 }) then
      no_inpaint = no_inpaint + 1
    end
  end
  if no_inpaint == 4 then
    local result = app.alert { title = "Missing inpainting", text = 'No area marked for inpainting. Paint in the "inpainting layer" to select which area the tool should modify', buttons = { "OK", "Help" } }

    if result == 2 then
      local url = "https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/getting-started"
      -- Open the URL in the default web browser
      if os.execute("start " .. url) == nil then
        if os.execute("xdg-open " .. url) == nil then
          if os.execute("open " .. url) == nil then
            print("Failed to open the URL.")
          end
        end
      end
    end
    return
  end


  local copy_data = createJson.deepcopy(model.current_json)
  -- model.current_json["selected_reference_image"] = selected_reference_image
  local jsonData = createJSON.create_with_size(model, copy_data,
    getImage.get_images_bytes_from_json(copy_data))

  if jsonData == nil then
    return
  end

  model["generation_start_frame"] = app.activeFrame.frameNumber
  if model.current_json["output_method"] == "New frame" then
    for index = 1, 3 do
      if app.activeFrame.next ~= nil then
        app.activeFrame = app.activeFrame.next
      end
    end
  end

  local cels = generate_movement.prepare_image(model, true)

  mask.move_mask_to_top()
  request_history.insert_request(copy_data.model_name, request_history_data)
  websocket.request(model, jsonData, _url .. "generate-movement", cels, dlg_type)

func validate_payload(payload):
	var current_project = ExtensionsApi.project.current_project
	var width = current_project.size.x
	var height = current_project.size.y
	var area = width * height


	if area > _get_max_area():
		ExtensionsApi.dialog.show_error("Canvas area too large. Maximum is 128x128")
		return false


	var valid_sizes = _get_valid_sizes()
	var target_size = max(_get_nearest_valid_size(width), _get_nearest_valid_size(height))

	if width != target_size or height != target_size:

		var dialog = ConfirmationDialog.new()
		dialog.title = "Pad Canvas"
		dialog.dialog_text = "The canvas must be %dx%d, %dx%d, or %dx%d pixels.\nYour canvas is %dx%d.\n\nWould you like to automatically pad the canvas to %dx%d?" % [
			valid_sizes[0], valid_sizes[0], 
			valid_sizes[1], valid_sizes[1], 
			valid_sizes[2], valid_sizes[2], 
			width, height, 
			target_size, target_size
		]
		dialog.confirmed.connect( func():
			var x_offset = (target_size - width) / 2
			var y_offset = (target_size - height) / 2


			DrawingAlgos.resize_canvas(target_size, target_size, x_offset, y_offset)

			dialog.queue_free()
		)
		dialog.canceled.connect( func():
			dialog.queue_free()
		)
		ExtensionsApi.dialog.get_dialogs_parent_node().add_child(dialog)
		dialog.popup_centered()
		return false

	return true

parameters.name: target
parameters.declaration: str (required) — Where to save it. A rotation: `character:<id>:<direction>`, `object:<id>:<direction>`, or `object:<id>` for a one-direction object.
